html:
This image was taken with a filter that lets hydrogen light through. Two nebulae located in the constellation Auriga are visible in it: IC405 at upper right and IC410 at lower left. These are nebulae made of clouds of ionized hydrogen atoms.


For this photo, here are the technical parameters
Date:  4 nights in 2010/12 and 2011/01
Optical train = Takahashi Sky90 + f4.5 reducer - Astronomik Ha 12nm filter - Canon xsi unfiltered
Mount: Takahashi EM-200 Temma II
Guided with Kwik Guider and the Phd software
Temperature: Variable from -5 to -15 deg
Site: At home
33 exposures of 20 minutes for 660 minutes
Dark, flat and bias applied
Calibration/Registration/Integration and processing in PixInsight
